chunks: From him, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

Regarding a man who was sitting with a group of people and then died while he was with them, or a man who was found in a tribe or at the door of a people’s house, and a claim was made against them, he said: “There is nothing upon them, and his blood is not to be left uncompensated.”

key_terms.دَمُهُ: his blood, meaning the legal right attached to the slain person
key_terms.فَادُّعِيَ: a claim or accusation was brought
key_terms.قَبِيلَةٍ: a tribe or communal setting in which a dead person is found
key_terms.قَوْمٍ: a group of people against whom suspicion or claim is made
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِمْ شَيْءٌ: no legal liability is established upon them on that basis alone
key_terms.يُطَلُّ: to be left unaddressed or uncompensated in blood-rights

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man is found dead among a group of people or at the door of a house and the killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a person found dead among a group or near a people’s dwelling when no known killer is identified. It states that liability is not established against them merely by such a claim, while also affirming that the victim’s blood is not to be left without due legal consideration.
